name: International Climbing and Mountaineering Federation
description: The UIAA is the international federation for mountaineering and climbing, representing over 90 member associations worldwide. It sets safety standards for climbing equipment, organizes international competitions, and advocates for mountain environment protection. The federation plays a key role in promoting safe and ethical mountaineering practices globally.

name: International Federation of Mountain Guides Associations
description: The IFMGA sets the international standard for mountain guide training and certification across 27 member countries. Their certified guides are recognized as the highest qualified professionals in mountaineering, skiing, and rock climbing instruction. The organization ensures consistent safety and competency standards worldwide.

name: American Alpine Club
description: The American Alpine Club is the leading national organization for climbers and mountaineers in the United States. It provides resources, grants, and rescue insurance to its members while maintaining an extensive mountaineering library and archive. The AAC publishes the annual American Alpine Journal, documenting significant ascents worldwide.

name: The Alpine Club
description: Founded in 1857, The Alpine Club is the world's oldest mountaineering club and has been at the heart of climbing history for over 165 years. Its members have included many of history's most famous mountaineers, from Edward Whymper to Chris Bonington. The club maintains an invaluable collection of mountaineering archives, art, and photographs.

name: Nepal Mountaineering Association
description: The Nepal Mountaineering Association manages climbing permits and regulations for peaks in Nepal under 6,500 meters. It promotes responsible mountaineering tourism and supports the training and welfare of Nepali climbing guides. The NMA works closely with the government to balance economic development with mountain conservation.

name: British Mountaineering Council
description: The BMC represents the interests of climbers, hill walkers, and mountaineers across England and Wales. With over 85,000 members, it campaigns for access to cliffs and mountains while providing travel insurance and training. The organization also plays a crucial role in maintaining climbing areas and publishing safety guidelines.

name: German Alpine Club
description: The DAV is one of the world's largest mountaineering and climbing organizations with over 1.4 million members. It maintains an extensive network of over 320 mountain huts across the Alps and operates hundreds of climbing facilities. The club is deeply committed to environmental conservation and sustainable mountain tourism.

name: Italian Alpine Club
description: The Club Alpino Italiano is one of the oldest alpine clubs in the world, with over 300,000 members across 500 local sections. It maintains a vast network of mountain refuges throughout the Italian Alps and Apennines. The CAI is also responsible for maintaining thousands of kilometers of marked hiking trails across Italy.

name: Himalayan Trust
description: Founded by Sir Edmund Hillary, the Himalayan Trust supports education, health, and conservation projects in the Sherpa communities of Nepal's Everest region. The organization has built over 40 schools and two hospitals in the Solu-Khumbu district. Its work continues Hillary's lifelong commitment to giving back to the people who helped him reach the summit.

name: International Commission for Alpine Rescue
description: ICAR is the worldwide organization for mountain rescue services, bringing together rescue organizations from over 35 countries. It develops best practices for mountain rescue techniques, avalanche rescue, and helicopter operations. The commission facilitates knowledge sharing and training standards to save lives in mountain environments.

name: Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee
description: The SPCC is dedicated to managing waste and environmental conservation in the Everest region of Nepal. The organization operates waste management systems at Everest Base Camp and along trekking routes, collecting tons of refuse annually. Their efforts have been instrumental in combating the pollution crisis on the world's highest peak.

name: Mountain Wilderness International
description: Mountain Wilderness is an international NGO dedicated to protecting mountain wilderness and promoting sustainable practices in mountain regions. Founded by prominent mountaineers including Reinhold Messner, the organization campaigns against overdevelopment and advocates for leaving mountains in their natural state. They have led successful campaigns to remove abandoned infrastructure from alpine environments.
